attachments.name: image0.jpeg
attachments.visualDescription: A scan of a book page, not a painting. A flat deep wine red field with three lines of cream serif type centred slightly above the middle: the quotation "I feel like I have spent much of my career pursued by bulldozers." attributed in bold to Charlie Rogers. Landscape format, no imagery, no signature.

attachments.name: Paul Wright.jpg
attachments.visualDescription: The filename is misleading: this is not a photograph of a person. It is a small reproduction of the painting itself, a snow covered back lane between brick terraced houses, back yard walls and doors picked out in green, blue, red and purple, with a tall church tower and spire in the centre distance and two small figures with a dog walking away up the lane. Cool greys and whites with warm brick reds; oil handling. Signed and dated lower left, GHRogers 1980. This is the image used on the cover of Pursued by Bulldozers.

attachments.name: Image.jpeg
attachments.visualDescription: Oil painting, photographed square on and cropped close to the picture edge. A brick terrace frontage with four adjoining front doors, cream, green, dark red and pale grey, each under a glazed fanlight and framed by white painted brick quoins, with stone steps down to the pavement. The green door stands ajar on a dark interior with a striped rug. Sash windows above, one with a blue plant pot on the sill. Muted plum and russet brickwork against cool grey stone. A faint signature and date sit in the bottom left corner.

attachments.name: Image.jpeg
attachments.visualDescription: Snow scene looking down a sloping shopping street, painted in washy watercolour and pen over pale board, though Brian labels the original oil on paper. A tall gable on the left carries a hand lettered sign reading CHRIST JESUS CAME INTO THE WORLD TO SAVE SINNERS, with shopfronts below and a BINGO sign and a CASTLE sign further down the hill. A woman in a long blue coat pushes a pram through deep snow with a child and a small dog beside her, and a man in a cap leans against a shop corner in the foreground. A dark stormy blue grey sky with chimney smoke fills the upper right. Signed lower left with the date 1970 and inscribed Bensham Road, Gateshead.

attachments.visualDescription: A colour photograph, portrait format, of the book standing upright on a gravel path in a park with an avenue of cherry trees in full pink blossom arching overhead. The dust jacket shows the snowy back lane cover painting and the title "Pursued by Bulldozers, the life and times of a Gateshead artist". Almost certainly Saltwell Park.

attachments.name: Charlie Rogers Christmas Card Selection.pdf
attachments.visualDescription: Not a single image. A five-page PDF presenting the Charlie Rogers Christmas card selection, one card design per page, each headed Charlie Rogers The Collection with the painting title, place, year and medium beneath and a copyright line for Charles Rogers Junior. The five reproduced works are The Monument with Snow, Newcastle-on-Tyne 1996 (watercolour), St Cuthbert’s Church, Gateshead-on-Tyne 1982 (oil), Bensham Road, Gateshead 1970 (watercolour), Street meeting with snow, Gateshead 1972 (watercolour) and Cotfield Street, Bensham, Gateshead-on-Tyne, undated (watercolour). The page images themselves did not render on read, only the caption text, so the artwork colouring has not been seen.

attachments.name: Image-1.jpg
attachments.visualDescription: A colour photograph of the book propped on a speckled terrazzo ledge inside a glazed Victorian market hall with a barrel vaulted iron and glass roof, red and white striped stall canopies and shoppers below. The hall is the Grainger Market, Newcastle, with Pumphrey's Coffee Room visible on the right.
attachments.subject: Book

attachments.name: image00001.jpg
attachments.visualDescription: Photograph of an unframed oil painting resting against a pale grey wall, with masking tape and paper scraps visible along the top edge of the board. The picture shows a row of eight men in flat caps, suits and waistcoats seated along a green park bench, one man standing at the far right with a hand on his hip, and a small black dog trotting across the pale blue grey foreground. Palette is dominated by greys and slate blues with strong pink, orange and red accents in the waistcoats and background wall. Signed lower right, GHRogers.

attachments.name: IMG_4874.jpeg
attachments.visualDescription: Colour photograph of the book lying open on an embroidered floral cloth, showing the half-title page reading CHARLIE ROGERS, PURSUED BY BULLDOZERS, COMPILED BY BRIAN RANKIN, EDITED BY ANNIE DOYLE, in deep wine red and black. A blind embossed roundel reading CHARLIE ROGERS 1930 - 2020 sits at the foot of the page next to a handwritten ink signature. An old wooden paintbrush lies diagonally across the page, and the facing page carries a black and white photograph of a brick back lane and yard door. This is the evidence for the embossed and signed special edition.

attachments.name: image.png
attachments.visualDescription: A colour photograph of a man in a black polo with the "Come view my art" logo, glasses and a grey beard, signing the title page of an open copy of the book at a table. A striped photo album, a burgundy leaflet with a black and white photograph, and newspaper are on the table, framed Rogers works on the wall behind.

attachments.name: IMG_3569.jpeg
attachments.visualDescription: Watercolour and pen study of a cafe shopfront set inside a dressed stone railway arch. The frontage is painted mid blue, with a white fascia lettered HIGH LEVEL CAFE, flanked by SANDWICHES TO CARRY OUT on the left and OUR MOTTO QUICK SERVICE on the right, and a Snack Bar sign in the right hand window. Red and white gingham half curtains hang in both windows and a pale wooden gate stands across the central doorway. A red pillar box and a yellow sign on a post sit to the right, on a loosely drawn flagstone pavement. Muted stone greys and ochres against the blue joinery. Signed lower left, GHRogers 1977, and inscribed POT-PIE BOB'S WELLINGTON ST. GATESHEAD.
